---
engine: markdown
title: "Supported formats"
---

`rush` reads and writes a wide range of data formats. The file extension
determines which reader or writer is used. To override it, pass the format's
name to `--input-format` (`-F`) or `--output-format` (`-O`).

| Format | Extensions | Name | Read | Write | Package |
|--------|------------|------|:----:|:-----:|---------|
| Delimited text | `.csv`, `.tsv` | `csv`, `tsv`, `delim` | yes | yes | readr |
| Parquet | `.parquet`, `.pq` | `parquet` | yes | yes | nanoparquet |
| JSON | `.json` | `json` | yes | yes | jsonlite |
| JSON Lines | `.jsonl`, `.ndjson` | `jsonl` | yes | yes | jsonlite |
| Excel | `.xlsx` | `xlsx` | yes | yes | readxl / writexl |
| Excel 97-2003 | `.xls` | `xlsx` | yes | no | readxl |
| ODS | `.ods` | `ods` | yes | yes | readODS |
| Arrow IPC | `.arrow`, `.ipc`, `.feather` | `arrow` | yes | yes | arrow |
| DuckDB | `.duckdb`, `.ddb` | `duckdb` | yes | yes | duckdb |
| SQLite | `.sqlite`, `.db` | `sqlite` | yes | yes | RSQLite |
| SPSS | `.sav`, `.zsav` | `sav`, `zsav` | yes | yes | haven |
| SPSS portable | `.por` | `por` | yes | no | haven |
| Stata | `.dta` | `dta` | yes | yes | haven |
| SAS | `.sas7bdat`, `.xpt` | `sas7bdat`, `xpt` | yes | yes | haven |
| RDS | `.rds` | `rds` | yes | yes | readr |
| YAML | `.yaml`, `.yml` | `yaml` | yes | yes | yaml |
| TOML | `.toml` | `toml` | yes | yes | RcppTOML |
| XML | `.xml` | `xml` | yes | yes | xml2 |
| Fixed-width | `.fwf` | `fwf` | yes | no | readr |
| FASTA | `.fasta`, `.fa`, `.fna` | `fasta` | yes | yes | microseq |
| FASTQ | `.fastq`, `.fq` | `fastq` | yes | yes | microseq |

Any other extension is read and written as CSV. Writing a format that `rush`
can only read, such as `-o data.xls`, is an error.

Any readable format can be converted to any writable format, either with
[`rush convert`](reference/convert.qmd) or by naming the output file of
another command. A database holds several tables, so it converts to another
database, to a spreadsheet with a sheet per table, or to one file per table
with an [output template](reference/convert.qmd#multiple-files-with-output-templates).

Plots have their own output formats (ANSI, ASCII, PNG, SVG, PDF, and more),
described in [`rush plot`](reference/plot.qmd#output).

## Format-specific documentation

Each format has its own page with examples:

- [Delimited (CSV/TSV)](formats/delimited.qmd): delimiters, headers, `--head`
- [Parquet](formats/parquet.qmd): columnar storage via nanoparquet
- [JSON / JSONL](formats/json.qmd): nested data, flattening, streaming
- [Excel / ODS](formats/excel.qmd): sheets, spreadsheets
- [Arrow IPC](formats/arrow.qmd): Feather / IPC format
- [DuckDB / SQLite](formats/databases.qmd): multi-table databases, combining files
- [Statistical (SPSS, Stata, SAS)](formats/statistical.qmd): labelled data via haven
- [Bioinformatics (FASTA/FASTQ)](formats/bioinformatics.qmd): sequence data
- [Structured (YAML, TOML, XML, RDS, FWF)](formats/structured.qmd): config files, serialization
